findings.title: Clean up client-specific FGAP v2 resources when a client is deleted
Guard against a missing resource-type resource before policy lookup
Avoid a full policy evaluation per client resource in getClientsWithPermission
Remove dead code and unused imports in ClientPermissionsV2
Fix Javadoc on void require* methods

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Clean up client-specific FGAP v2 resources when a client is deleted

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:77-95
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:192-195

Explanation:
`ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. To avoid that exception, the listener body is now wrapped in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)`.

This means nothing happens when a client is removed under FGAP v2. The per-client `Resource` created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` stays in the admin-permissions resource server. Any scope permissions that point to it also stay. These orphaned resources and permissions pile up, show up in the permission listings, and can affect evaluation and listing.

There is also a second risk. If a deployment has both the v1 and v2 features enabled, `management(...)` may return `MgmtPermissionsV2` (this depends on code outside the diff). In that case `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...)` would throw while the client is being removed, and the client deletion would fail.

Fix: handle `ClientRemovedEvent` explicitly for v2. Remove or detach the client's resource from the admin-permissions resource server. Do not call the v1-only API in that path.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
if (event instanceof ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent cast) {
    if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2)) {
        // AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.removeResource(cast.getKeycloakSession(), cast.getClient()) ...
    } else if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) {
        management(cast.getKeycloakSession(), cast.getClient().getRealm()).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false);
    }
}
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Guard against a missing resource-type resource before policy lookup

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:214-224

Explanation:
When there is no per-client resource, the code calls `getResourceTypeResource(...)` and passes the result straight into `findByResource(server, resource)`. Later it also uses `resource.getScopes()`.

If the "Clients" type resource is absent, this could throw a `NullPointerException`. That could happen, for example, in a realm whose resource server was created before the `CLIENTS` type was added to the schema. Whether it can actually be null depends on `getResourceTypeResource`, which is outside the diff.

The `hasPermission(String)` overload already null-checks its resource. This overload should do the same.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);
if (resource == null || authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) {
    return false;
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Avoid a full policy evaluation per client resource in getClientsWithPermission

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:124-145

Explanation:
This method runs a separate `root.evaluatePermission(...)` for every resource of type `Clients`. In realms with many client-specific permissions, this costs N full policy evaluations per client-list request.

It also collects `resource.getName()` for every typed resource. If the "Clients" type resource itself has type `Clients`, the literal string "Clients" ends up in the returned ID set.

Fix:
- Evaluate in batch, passing multiple `ResourcePermission`s to a single evaluation.
- Skip the type resource, i.e. any resource whose name equals the type.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, resource -> {
    if (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE.equals(resource.getName())) return;
    if (hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)) granted.add(resource.getName());
});
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove dead code and unused imports in ClientPermissionsV2

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:22-23
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:46
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:262-272
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:207-286

Explanation:
- `getEvaluationContext` is a private method that is never called. It appears to be copied token-exchange logic, and token exchange is explicitly unsupported in V2.
- The `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `ClientModelIdentity` and `DefaultEvaluationContext` imports are therefore unused.
- `hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)`, `hasPermission(String)` and `hasGrantedPermission` repeat the same scope-matching loop. Each also wraps a single scope in `Arrays.asList` for no reason.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// delete getEvaluationContext and the unused imports; factor the loop:
private boolean evaluate(ResourceServer server, Resource resource, String scope) {
    return root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server), server)
            .stream().flatMap(p -> p.getScopes().stream()).anyMatch(scope::equals);
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Doc
Title: Fix Javadoc on void require* methods

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionEvaluator.java:95-103

Explanation:
`requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` return `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`. Their Javadoc nevertheless says "Returns {@code true} if ...", which contradicts the signatures. The other `require*` methods are documented correctly.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
/**
 * Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}.
 */
void requireView();

/**
 * Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code false}.
 */
void requireViewClientScopes();
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Restore realm state mutated by the new client permission tests

Affected:
- tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:166-178
- tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:330-341

Explanation:
The tests change the shared managed realm and never undo the changes:
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient`, removes one of its default client scopes, and adds it as an optional scope.
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles and assigns them to `myadmin`.

The `@AfterEach` only deletes permissions. Because of this, other tests can break depending on run order. For example, `defaultClientScopes.get(1)` assumes at least two default scopes, and re-creating `myclient-role` would fail with 409.

Register cleanup with `realm.cleanup()` or revert the changes in `@AfterEach`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().deleteRole("myclient-role"));
realm.cleanup().add(r -> r.clients().get(myclient.getId()).roles().deleteRole("myclient-subRole"));
// and restore name / default client scope for myclient after testManageOnlyOneClient
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Test
Title: Do not send a null body when asserting forbidden client creation

Affected:
- tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:319-322

Explanation:
`clients().create(null)` only returns 403 if the authorization check happens before the request body is processed. If the endpoint or its validation order changes, this will return 400 or 500, and the test will fail or pass for the wrong reason.

Use a valid representation so the test actually exercises the authorization decision.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
ClientRepresentation rep = new ClientRepresentation();
rep.setClientId("notAllowed");
try (Response response = realmAdminClient.realm(realm.getName()).clients().create(rep)) {
    Assertions.assertEquals(Status.FORBIDDEN.getStatusCode(), response.getStatus());
}
~~~

false_negatives.golden_comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.
